paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Lily and Leo found a leaflet in the town library. Its title was "Town Arts Days." The leaflet was blue and yellow, and it had a picture of a dancer. "Look at this!" said Leo. "There is a film, a dance show, and a leather workshop." Lily's mom stood next to them and read the leaflet, too.

The first page gave the days and the hours. "Open: Saturday, January second, and Sunday, January third." "Time: from ten o'clock to six o'clock." "Buy your tickets at the door." "Tickets: children, forty baht; adults, eighty baht." "Even a baby may come, and a baby needs no ticket." "How much are three tickets for us?" asked Leo. "Two children and one adult," said Lily's mom. "That is forty and forty and eighty, so it is one hundred sixty baht."

The second page told about the shows. "Dance show: eleven o'clock and three o'clock. Dancers from the town school." "Film room: an action film at one o'clock." "The film is thirty minutes long." "Leather workshop: make a bookmark." "Extra: thirty baht." "Leo wants to see the action film," said Lily. "I want to see the dancers," she added. "Then we can see the dancers at eleven o'clock and the film at one o'clock," said Mom.

On the back page, there was a box about the town TV channel. "Visit the studio of the town TV channel at two o'clock." "See how people make the news." The picture showed a small studio with a big green screen. "Leather bookmarks are a good gift," said Leo. "I will make one for my grandma." "May we see all of it in one day?" asked Lily. "Yes," said Mom, "but we must start early."

The last lines of the leaflet gave the rules. "Visitors may take photos, but they may not use a flash." "No food in the film room." "Children under ten must stay with an adult." "That is easy," said Lily, and she smiled at her mom. "Can we take the leaflet home?" asked Leo. "Yes," said Mom, "it is free." Lily put the leaflet in her bag and smiled.
